 Order

Accused No.1 in Crime No.314/2022 registered by Pulakeshinagara Police Station, Bengaluru City for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A), 304(B) R/w Sections 3, 4 & 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 is before this Court seeking regular bail.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State.
3.

On the basis of complaint lodged by Sri Chikkanarasaih S/o Late Narasimhaiah dated 13.10.2022,
FIR in Crime No.314/2022 was registered by Pulakeshinagara Police against the petitioner herein and 3 others for the aforesaid offences.
In the complaint it is averred that, the complainant's daughter Manjula was married to the petitioner herein on 28.11.2021 at Tumakuru.
At the time of the marriage, the complainant had given dowry as per the demand made by the petitioner and his family members.
After the marriage there was constant ill-treatment and torture to the daughter of the complainant.
On 11.10.2022, the complainant was informed by the petitioner that his daughter had consumed rat poison and NC: 2023:KHC:33387 she was shifted to Bowring hospital.
The complainant went to the hospital and found that his daughter Manjula was admitted in the hospital.
Subsequently, Manjula was shifted to Jain hospital.
She died in the said hospital during the course of treatment on 13.10.2022.
Thereafter, the complainant had approached the police and lodged the complaint which had resulted in registering FIR in Crime No.314/2022 .
During the course of investigation, the petitioner was arrested on 14.10.2022.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.

The bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C, filed by the petitioner before the court of LXXI Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City in Crl.Misc.No.1465/2023 was dismissed on 23.02.2023.

sentences.text: It is under these circumstances, the petitioner is before this court.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner reiterated the grounds urged in the petition and submits that the petitioner is in custody since 14.10.2022.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State has opposed the bail application.

From a perusal of the complaint averments it is seen that, omnibus allegations are made against the petitioner and other accused persons with regard to demand of dowry and harassment meted out on Manjula by the accused persons.
There are no particulars of any specific incident of harassment or ill-treatment narrated in the complaint.

On 11.10.2022 Manjula had consumed rat Manjanna vs State Of Karnataka on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137908579/
2 poison and she was immediately shifted to hospital by the petitioner and thereafter the petitioner had informed the complainant about the same.

sentences.text: From 11.10.2022 till 13.10.2022 Manjula, was admitted in the hospital.
In the meanwhile, no complaint has been filed regarding ill-treatment by the accused persons on Manjula.
It is only after Manjula died, the complainant had approached the police and lodged the complaint.

For the purpose of attracting offence punishable under section 304B of IPC, husband or his relatives should have ill-treat or torture the deceased immediately prior to she committing the act of suicide, in furtherance of the demand for dowry.
No such ingredient is found in the complaint.
The petitioner is in custody since 14.10.2022.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.

Under these circumstances, I am of the NC:
2023:KHC:33387 considered view that the petitioner's prayer for grant of regular bail is required to be considered favourably.
In view of the above, the petition is allowed.
d ) The petitioner shall not leave the  jurisdiction of the Trial Court without  NC: 2023:KHC:33387 permission of the said Court until the case registered against him is disposed off.
